info.name: RAUW Backend API
info.description: Backend-only RAUW API collection. Starts with bearer token authentication requests and can be expanded as new backend endpoints are added.

item.name: Auth

exec: pm.test('Response contains bearer token and officer profile', function () {

request.description: Register a backend API-only officer account with username, email, password, confirm_password, badge_number, department_ids, and optional district_ids. department_ids is required, must contain at least one existing department ID, and cannot contain duplicates; officers must have one or more departments. district_ids may be omitted or empty, must contain active existing district IDs when present, and cannot contain duplicates; assignments are stored through district_officer. The 201 response includes token_type, access_token, actor_type, and a cleaned safe officer profile with departments and districts as compact arrays. The test script stores access_token in collection and active environment variables. Change username, email, and badge_number before rerunning because username and badge_number must be unique within officers and email must be unique across users, officers, and managers.

exec: pm.test('Response contains bearer token and user profile', function () {

request.description: Register a public API user account with name, username, email, password, and confirm_password. The 201 response includes token_type, access_token, actor_type, and a cleaned safe user profile that does not duplicate actor_type or expose internal auth fields. The test script stores access_token in collection and active environment variables. Change username and email before rerunning because username must be unique within users and email must be unique across users, officers, and managers.

exec: pm.test('Response contains bearer token and profile', function () {

request.description: Authenticate with email and password only. The response includes token_type, access_token, actor_type, and a cleaned profile. actor_type is only present at the top level; profile omits internal auth fields. Officer and manager profiles expose assigned departments and districts as compact arrays. The test script stores access_token in collection and active environment variables.

Return the authenticated actor_type and cleaned safe profile payload. actor_type is only present at the top level; profile omits internal auth fields. Officer and manager profiles expose assigned departments and districts as compact arrays. Requires Authorization: Bearer <token>.
Revoke the bearer token used by this request. Requires Authorization: Bearer <token>.

item.description: Authentication requests for user, officer, and manager actors.

item.name: Managers

exec: pm.test('Response contains created manager profile only', function () {

request.description: Create an ordinary manager as the authenticated main manager. Requires Authorization: Bearer <token> from an active manager with is_main_manager=true. department_ids is required, must contain at least one existing department ID, and cannot contain duplicates; manager department assignments are stored through the department_manager pivot. Optional district_ids must contain active existing districts and are stored through district_manager. The 201 response returns the created manager profile only, including departments and districts as compact arrays, and does not include or store an access_token. The new manager must log in separately through Auth / Login. Change username and email before rerunning because username must be unique within managers and email must be unique across users, officers, and managers.

Implemented self-service district assignment endpoint for active managers and active officers. Replace the authenticated actor's own district assignments. Users do not have district assignments and receive 403. district_ids must be present, may be an empty array to clear assignments, must contain active existing district IDs, and cannot contain duplicates. Returns the refreshed auth profile with a districts array. This only updates actor district pivots and never modifies issues.district_id.

Manager-admin district assignment endpoint. Replace an officer's district assignments as an authenticated active manager. Users, officers, inactive managers, and unauthenticated requests cannot update officer districts. district_ids must be present, may be empty to clear assignments, must contain active existing district IDs, and cannot contain duplicates. Returns the officer's refreshed profile with districts. This only updates district_officer and never modifies issues.district_id.

Planned main-manager-only department assignment endpoint (not yet in routes/api.php). Replace an officer's department assignments as an authenticated active main manager (is_main_manager=true). Users, officers, ordinary managers, inactive managers, inactive main managers, and unauthenticated requests receive 403. Unlike Update Officer Districts, non-main managers cannot call this endpoint. department_ids must be present, may be an empty array to clear assignments, must reference existing department IDs from the departments table, and cannot contain duplicates. Returns the officer's refreshed auth profile (actor_type + profile) with departments. Soft-deleted officers return 404. This only updates department_officer.

Planned main-manager-only department assignment endpoint (not yet in routes/api.php). Replace a manager's department assignments as an authenticated active main manager. department_ids must be present, may be [] to clear all assignments, must reference existing department IDs, and cannot contain duplicates. Returns the refreshed Manager resource (flat manager profile with departments and districts). Soft-deleted managers return 404. Use the main manager token from Auth / Login (demo.manager@example.com locally).

item.description: Protected manager administration requests. Manager creation is restricted to authenticated active main managers. District assignment requests include implemented manager self-service updates and manager-admin officer district updates. Department assignment PATCH requests are spec-first until backend routes ship; they require an active main manager token.

item.name: Officers

request.description: Implemented officer self-service district assignment flow. Replace the authenticated officer's district assignments through district_officer. district_ids must be an array of active existing district IDs without duplicates; use an empty array to clear assignments. Returns the refreshed auth profile with districts and never modifies issues.district_id.

item.description: Officer-focused request examples. The district self-service update entry is implemented for active officers.

item.name: Categories

request.description: List categories as an authenticated active manager. Main categories are ordered by priority and children by weight; lower numbers mean higher priority. Responses include assigned departments from the category_department pivot.
Show one category with parent, children when loaded, and assigned departments. Requires an authenticated active manager.
Create a main category as an authenticated active manager. Main categories use priority; lower values sort first. department_ids must contain existing departments.
Create a subcategory under an active main category. Nested subcategories are rejected. Subcategories use weight; lower values sort first.
Partially update a category as an authenticated active manager. If department_ids is present, it replaces the category's pivot assignments.
Standard safe removal path. Sets is_active=false while keeping the category row, department assignments, and historical issue references intact.
Guarded hard delete for eligible categories only. Prefer Disable Category. A main category with subcategories returns 409, and categories referenced by existing issues also return 409.

item.description: Category management requests. Requires an authenticated active manager. Categories are assigned to departments through a many-to-many pivot. Disable is the standard removal path; hard delete is guarded.

item.name: Districts

request.description: List districts ordered by name with manager/officer assignment counts and issue reference counts. Requires authentication in the protected API group. Managers and officers use many-to-many district pivots; issues.district_id remains a singular issue location/reference field.
Show one district with manager/officer assignment counts and issue reference count. Requires authentication.
Create a district as an authenticated active manager. Users, officers, inactive managers, and unauthenticated requests cannot create districts.
Update a district as an authenticated active manager. Supports partial updates for name, postal_prefix, center_lat, center_lng, radius_meters, and is_active.

Delete an eligible district as an authenticated active manager. Returns 409 Conflict while the district is assigned to managers, assigned to officers, or referenced by issues through issues.district_id.

item.description: District CRUD requests. Reads require authentication; mutations require an authenticated active manager. Actor district assignments are many-to-many through district_manager and district_officer. Issue district handling is out of scope: issues.district_id remains singular.

item.name: Issues

exec: pm.test('Issue has derived departments, required district, and safe author', function () {

body.raw:
{
  "title": "Losliggende stoeptegel",
  "content": "Er ligt een stoeptegel los bij de bushalte.",
  "category_id": {{category_id}},
  "district_id": {{district_id}},
  "postal_code": "3241AB",
  "address": "Voorstraat 1, Middelharnis",
  "latitude": 51.7575,
  "longitude": 4.165,
  "is_anonymous": true
}

request.description: Create an issue as an authenticated active user. Required fields are title, content, category_id, and district_id. Do not send department: issue departments are derived server-side from the selected category, stored through the department_issue pivot, and returned as a read-only departments array. Optional location fields are postal_code, address, latitude, and longitude. Removed legacy locality fields are not accepted. Anonymous issues remain owned through issues.user_id; the backend generates a stable alias such as Melder#A1B2C3D4 and does not accept anonymous_alias from clients. The test stores issue_id for follow-up requests.

query.description: Composable filter by real department code; matches issues where any assigned department has this code

request.description: List issues for an authenticated actor. district_id, department, and category_id are optional and composable; combine any subset to narrow results. The department query value must be an existing department code and is applied through the issue departments relationship with any-match semantics, so a multi-department issue is returned when any assigned department matches. Pagination is backend-driven with page and per_page; per_page defaults to 20 and is capped at 100.

Show one issue with derived read-only departments plus category, district, and attachment summaries when loaded. The response exposes departments as an array only and does not include a singular department field. Authenticated request only. Anonymous issues expose an author display alias and not the owning user id.

body.raw:
{
  "title": "Stoeptegel bij bushalte bijgewerkt",
  "content": "De tegel ligt nu volledig los.",
  "category_id": {{category_id}},
  "district_id": {{district_id}},
  "is_anonymous": false
}

request.description: Partially update an issue owned by the authenticated active user. Ownership is checked through issues.user_id, including anonymous issues. Editable fields are title, content, category_id, district_id, postal_code, address, latitude, longitude, and is_anonymous. Do not send department: when category_id changes, departments are re-derived from that category and returned as a read-only departments array. Attachments are changed separately: delete existing attachments first when replacement is needed, then use Upload Attachments.

exec: pm.test('Response wraps attachments in data array', function () {

formdata.description: Choose 1-5 files. Each file must be <= 5 MB and one of jpg, jpeg, png, gif, webp, or pdf.

request.description: Upload attachments to an issue owned by the authenticated active user. Each issue may hold at most 5 attachments total. Each file is limited to 5 MB. Files are stored on local non-public development storage and are downloaded only through authenticated endpoints. The 201 response wraps attachments as data: [...]. The test stores attachment_id and attachment_download_url from response.data[0].

Owner-only attachment deletion. Requires Authorization: Bearer <token> for the active regular user who owns the issue. The attachment must belong to the issue in the route. A successful request returns 204 No Content, removes the backing file from non-public local storage when present, and hard deletes the attachment row. Use before Upload Attachments when replacing files.
Authenticated attachment download. The attachment must belong to the issue in the route and the local backing file must exist. The API streams the original filename from non-public local storage.

Hard delete an issue owned by the authenticated active user. This is not a soft delete: the issue row is removed and attachments cascade with the issue. Run after attachment examples if you want to preserve issue_id for follow-up requests.

item.description: Authenticated issue CRUD and attachment examples. Issue creation requires district_id and no longer accepts client-supplied department or removed legacy locality fields. Departments are derived from the selected category, stored in department_issue, and exposed as a read-only departments array. List filters are composable; department filtering uses real department codes with any-match semantics, and pagination is backend-driven. Anonymous issues retain user_id ownership while exposing only a stable alias. Attachment deletion is owner-only for replacement workflows. Issue deletion is hard delete and attachments cascade with the issue.

item.name: Departments

request.description: List departments from the departments table with category counts. Requires authentication in the protected API group.
Show one department with category count. Requires authentication in the protected API group.

Create a department. Requires an authenticated active main manager (is_main_manager=true). Ordinary managers, users, officers, inactive managers, and unauthenticated requests cannot mutate departments.
Update a department. Requires an authenticated active main manager.

Delete a department as an authenticated active main manager. Departments assigned to any manager or officer return 409 until those actor assignments are changed. After no actors reference the department, database cascade removes category_department and department_issue assignments automatically; category and issue records remain intact.

item.description: Department CRUD requests. Department mutations require an authenticated active main manager. Managers use department_ids through the department_manager pivot and must have one or more departments; officers use department_ids through the department_officer pivot and must have one or more departments. Deleting a department is blocked while assigned to managers or officers; otherwise it removes category_department and department_issue pivot assignments automatically but does not delete categories or issues. Issue departments are derived from categories and exposed to clients as read-only departments arrays.
